raw_response:
My reasoning:

I am 68, but only started farming this land one year ago. My son works in the city and I took over. I do not know everything yet, so I watch what my neighbors do and ask the old men at the village shop. They have farmed here all their lives. Whatever most of them do, that is what I do. Changing too much is how you lose a harvest, and at my age I cannot afford a bad year.

My 10.1 mu is split. About 3 mu I keep in cotton because the soil there is a bit sandy and my wife knows how to pick it. The other 7.1 mu I do wheat in winter and maize in summer, same as almost everyone in the village.

For wheat, I plant in October. I buy improved seed from the agro shop — the owner tells me which variety the neighbors buy, I get the same. For base fertilizer I put down 2 bags of 二铵 (DAP, 50 jin each) per mu before ploughing, then at greening (返青) I broadcast about 1 bag of urea per mu. That works out to around 25 jin of nitrogen, 8 jin phosphorus, 6 jin potassium per mu. I water 3 times — winter water before freezing, then at jointing, then at grain-fill. I spray twice, once for aphids and yellow rust, once for the grain. I hope for 500 jin per mu; my neighbor got 550 last year but he has done it longer.

For maize, I direct-seed right after wheat harvest in June. Hybrid seed, 郑单958 — everyone plants it. I put a bag of compound (15-15-15) at sowing, then side-dress urea at the big trumpet stage, maybe 25 jin urea per mu. Two waterings, one spray for corn borer. I aim for 550 jin.

For cotton, I use Bt seed from the shop — the old kind has too many bollworms. I give it more fertilizer because cotton is greedy. Three irrigations, and I must spray 4-5 times for aphids, spider mites, bollworms. I hope for 220 jin seed cotton per mu. It is more work than grain but the price is better.

I do rotary tillage — the tractor man comes, 40 yuan per mu, fast and easy for an old man like me.
